cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example, at the four decimals its description publishes
cases.expected_note: Microsoft publishes =TBILLYIELD(A2,A3,A4) with the description "The yield for the Treasury bill using the terms in A2, A3, and A4 (0.0914, or 9.14%)" and a Result cell formatted as "9.14%". Settlement 2008-03-31, maturity 2008-06-01, price $98.45 per $100 face value. DERIVATION (the page's formula is an image, awftbyd.gif, with the same DSM legend): (100 - pr)/pr * (360/DSM) with the ACTUAL day count 62 gives 0.09141696292534281361097, i.e. 0.0914 at the published precision. Microsoft's page was read live on 2026-08-31 at https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/functions/tbillyield-function. FETCH NOTE FOR THIS BATCH: batch F recorded every /en-us/office/<name>-function-<guid> URL returning Microsoft's 'Sorry, the page you're looking for can't be found' body; today BOTH paths serve the article again -- the GUID form redirects to /en-us/excel/functions/<slug>-function -- and every page cited in this batch came back complete (217-223 KB) in one or two attempts, with no 87 KB stub responses. Nothing here is sourced from a search snippet or a mirror.

cases.description: The same example carried to ten decimals
cases.expected_note: Asserted at ten places from the derivation: 0.0914169629. Four published decimals cannot separate the actual day count from the 30/360 one here either (61 days would give 0.0929), though in this case the difference is larger than it is for TBILLEQ.

cases.description: A price of zero, which the page excludes
cases.expected_note: The Remarks publish: "If pr <= 0, TBILLYIELD returns the #NUM! error value." The formula divides by pr, so zero would be a division by zero as well as a documented exclusion.

cases.description: Settlement equal to maturity, which THIS page excludes with >= where its two siblings use >
cases.expected_note: A DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE THREE TBILL PAGES, recorded because it is testable. TBILLYIELD's Remark publishes "If settlement >= maturity, or if maturity is more than one year after settlement, TBILLYIELD returns the #NUM! error value" -- with a GREATER-THAN-OR-EQUAL -- while TBILLEQ and TBILLPRICE both publish "If settlement > maturity". Equal dates are therefore documented as an error here and not documented as one on the other two pages; the arithmetic agrees, since DSM = 0 would divide by zero. Only TBILLYIELD's file asserts this case, because only TBILLYIELD's page states it.

cases.description: A maturity more than a year after settlement, which the page excludes
cases.expected_note: The second half of the same Remark.
The Remarks publish: "If settlement or maturity is not a valid date, TBILLYIELD returns the #VALUE! error value."
